mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate compresses equity discount rates, increasing present value of future cash flows and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days without threshold requirements.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Declining unemployment rate signals stronger labor market conditions and rising corporate profit margins, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over 20 days without requiring specific thresholds.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE is below 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts exceeding 1.25 million units indicates robust consumer spending and economic expansion, triggering positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when HOUST exceeds 1250.0.

mechanism_narrative: Manufacturing production index above 109.5 signals strong industrial output and rising corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO exceeds 109.5.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous federal funds rate below 2.5% and unemployment below 4.0% creates a dual stimulus of cheap capital and tight labor markets, producing positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
regime_hint: monetary easing with tight labor market
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when both FEDFUNDS < 2.5 and UNRATE < 4.0.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent housing starts above 1.25 million and manufacturing production above 109.5 indicate synchronized economic strength, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when both HOUST > 1250.0 and INDPRO > 109.5.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS rising at least 0.5% in 3 months), increased discount rates and reduced liquidity cause negative S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods during a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS rise ≥0.5% in 3 months).

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansions with unemployment below 4.0%, overheating concerns and policy tightening lead to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE is below 4.0% during late-cycle expansion.
